title: Storyboard journey of a Claude Code mod
description: Every screen (node) and every key (edge) of one mod design, on fixture worlds (scenarios). Read by scripts/journey-lint.py, scripts/crawl.py and scripts/storyboard-build.py. Procedure: references/storyboard.md.

title.description: Page title of the player, for example 'my-mod · design C storyboard'.

notes.description: Free text for the reviewer: size, design rules that differ from the real code, what is not in the storyboard.

crawl.description: Defaults for crawl.py. A command-line option wins over a value here.

command.description: Template of the reset command. {mod} = plugin name, {scenario} = scenario id. Default '/{mod} {scenario}'.

paneColumn.description: First column of the pane body (the column right of the dock divider). 0 = the whole screen. Left out = find the divider on each screen.

clearScenarios.description: Scenarios whose edge replays start with /clear (old transcript lines would match their markers). Node captures always start with /clear.

openMarker.description: Text that shows only while the pane is open. Used, with the dock divider, to decide whether a reset must send Esc.

ringAreas.description: Areas whose captures get the ring check when a ❯ shows. Left out = every area.

keyTimeout.description: Seconds to wait for a marker after a key. Default 7.

waitTimeout.description: Seconds to wait for a marker after a 'wait' key. Default 14.

pointer.description: The selection pointer the design draws, for the ring check. Default '❯'.

hints.description: Rules that turn a hint on the screen into a key. Replaces the default rules when given.

re.description: Python regex. The match is the hotspot. Group 1, when there is one and 'key' is not given, is the key.

key.description: The edge key token this hint stands for (Escape, Enter, Down, Tab, C-x ...).

extraHints.description: Rules added to the defaults (same shape as 'hints').

ignore.description: Python regexes. A hint match that sits inside a match of one of these does not count (for example the active tab '▸ 1: Result').

same.description: Key groups that count as one key, for example [['Up','Down']]. Default [['Up','Down']].

description.description: The fixture world in plain words: what data, what timers, what each action returns.

group.description: Group name in the player's scenario menu.

area.description: The view or surface: list, detail, settings, band, toast ...

description.description: What the screen shows, with its exact hint footer.

scenario.description: The scenario where the node is first reached.

marker.description: Texts joined by ' && '. A part that starts with '!' must not show. Only this node satisfies it.

source.description: Where the screen comes from: spec section, file:line of the handler or the prototype.

focus.description: Text that the focus ring (inverse run) must hold on this screen, for example 'n: keep it' on a confirm (the safe choice). crawl.py fails the capture when it does not.

region.description: Where the marker is searched. 'screen' for a band, a toast or a transcript line. Default: 'pane' when a pane is open, else 'screen'.

key.description: tmux send-keys names, space-separated. 'K*N' = K pressed N times. 'text:"..."' = literal text; {mod} in it becomes the plugin name. 'wait' = send nothing, wait for a timer.

label.description: What the key does, in plain words.

source.description: The handler: file:line of onPress, onSubmit, hotkey, ui.close ...

scn.description: Replay this edge in this scenario. It also limits the edge to this scenario when the crawler finds a path.

onlyIn.description: Path search may use this edge only in these scenarios.

notIn.description: Path search must not use this edge in these scenarios.

history.description: true = the result depends on where you came from (Esc back to the origin, a kept draft). Path search never uses it; the crawler checks it on the route via the target.

approx.description: The target is the nearest captured screen, not the exact one. The note says what differs.

check.description: Marker that must hold after the key, instead of the target's marker. Required with 'approx' when the target marker does not hold.

timeout.description: Seconds to wait for the marker after this key (a long fixture timer).

skip.description: Source lines with no node or edge on purpose: a piece of the line text -> why.
